newsitem.title: USA: Key issues on EU's Fischler, US's Glickman agenda.
newsitem.headline: Key issues on EU's Fischler, US's Glickman agenda.

text.p: The top agriculture policymakers for the United States and the European Union faced an agenda filled with major issues Monday, aides said.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman was expected to raise the issues of bio-engineered crops and labeling rules for them, lingering questions on a meat inspection pact reached earlier this year, and EU use of export taxes and subsidies.
"We will want to raise the (beef) hormone issue," a Glickman aide said, but noted Franz Fischler, the EU agriculture commissioner, might not be ready for a discussion.
Fischler and Glickman met at 1120 EDT/1520 GMT.

An EU official told reporters earlier in the day that the hormone issue would be off the table because a World Trade Organization ruling was not official yet. A WTO panel has decided the EU was improperly blocking imports of U.S. beef grown with the aid of synthetic growth hormones.
The EU was expected to appeal the ruling.

Before the meeting, Fischler said he expected discussions on biotech crops, labeling rules, wheat export taxes and a proposed wine agreement. The wine agreement would spell out the nomenclature, such as champagne, that growers could to their wines.
